transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-11
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 55 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (CSM), Marco Alvarez (SE); Maya Chen, Carlos Ruiz, Leah Thompson, Aaron Patel (Aegis)
Recording link: https://redwood-recordings.example/ff/ff-2027-02-11-4729 (note: link placeholder)

Summary (auto): Quick kickoff, agree pilot scope and next steps.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, I'm the AE on the account. With me are Priya who's our CSM, and Marco our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing at Aegis?
[00:07] Maya Chen: Good, thanks. Excited to get started. We've been looking forward to this.
[00:10] Carlos Ruiz: Yep, thanks for setting up. We want to align on timeline and security first.
[00:15] Jordan Lee: Totally. Today's goal is a quick kickoff: confirm stakeholders, run through onboarding plan, and then set immediate action items - sandbox, SSO, and a tech deep dive to run initial benchmarks.
[00:28] Priya Nair: I'll own the onboarding workspace and day-to-day tasks. Marco will take the technical side like perf and integration.
[00:34] Leah Thompson: Quick note: our infra team is stretched this quarter so we want as little ops friction as possible. Hosted would be preferred unless we need dedicated for compliance.
[00:42] Marco Alvarez: Understood. We can map options. Quick caveat: dedicated capacity (we sometimes call it Redwood DedicaTed on docs, lol) gives predictable throughput but has infra commitments; private/VPC is the most locked down but more setup.
[00:57] Aaron Patel: On the security side, we need SOC 2 evidence, SAML SSO, audit logs and KMS integration for key control, and data residency in our US region.
[01:08] Jordan Lee: Great checklist - all standard for enterprise. We have a SOC 2 summary and ISO docs, and we support SAML-based SSO + SCIM for provisioning. For keys, Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Private and Dedicated flows; for hosted we provide envelope encryption with dedicated KMS options for enterprise. I'll share the security pack after the call.
[01:28] Maya Chen: Awesome. For the pilot we plan to test semantic search and document summarization across medical notes; we'll supply a sample dataset. Latency targets are 200-300ms for 95th perc on short prompts, throughput about 100 qps for batch jobs. Can you meet that?
[01:46] Marco Alvarez: That's achievable with the right model variant and batching. We'll recommend a quantized variant for cost and a lower-latency kernel; for 95th at 200-300ms we might be in a dedicated config or hosted with reserved throughput. We'll propose exact sku in the perf plan.
[02:03] Carlos Ruiz: Cost is important too. We want to compare against our current OpenAI spend - hopefully Redwood's batching/caching will show savings.
[02:10] Jordan Lee: Yep, Redwood's Optimize tooling and automatic prefix KV caching usually reduces per-token cost significantly for repeat contexts. We'll include a cost comparison in the follow-up deck.
[02:20] Priya Nair: Regarding timeline, we usually do: sandbox provisioning (1 week), initial perf/accuracy run (2 weeks), pilot (4 weeks), then rollout. Does that align with your timelines?
[02:30] Maya Chen: That aligns. We want pilot results before end of Q1.
[02:33] Jordan Lee: Sounds good.

[02:45] (Section: Roles and responsibilities)
[02:46] Jordan Lee: Priya will run onboarding tasks and Monday syncs. Marco will handle the integration and perf runs. Maya/Carlos/Leah are primary contacts at Aegis. Aaron is security.
[02:58] Leah Thompson: We'll need service account details and an IP allowlist for any VPC peering testing.
[03:04] Marco Alvarez: Noted. For VPC/private setups we can support VPC peering or private endpoints. For hosted access we can IP allowlist and TLS mutual auth if needed.

[03:20] (Short demo/overview: 3:20-10:00)
[03:21] Marco Alvarez: I'll run a 6-minute overview of the console so you know where things live - model catalog, routes, and the observability console.
[03:30] Marco Alvarez: (screen share noises) So here's the model catalog; we surface performance profiles and an ops dashboard. Note that sometimes the names in the transcription show our old internal names, like 'Redwood Run' or 'red ded' in older decks, ignore that.
[03:52] Maya Chen: The tracing and token-cost breakdown look useful. Can we export traces to our Splunk?
[03:57] Marco Alvarez: Yes, we have hooks to send traces and logs to external observability - Splunk, Datadog, or S3.
[04:04] Aaron Patel: How long is log retention? We need 1 year for audit logs behind enterprise plan.
[04:09] Priya Nair: Enterprise retention add-on supports 1 year and longer; I will include pricing.
[04:14] Carlos Ruiz: Also: does the console show per-route SLA and automatic fallbacks? We need deterministic behavior if a model goes down.
[04:21] Marco Alvarez: Yes - rollouts include canarying and automatic fallback to compatible model variants and regions. We can set routing policies by latency or cost.

[04:40] (Questions from Aegis)
[04:42] Maya Chen: A few specifics: 1) For PII in medical notes, does Redwood store raw payloads? 2) For private deployment, is customer data ever shared with other tenants?
[04:52] Jordan Lee: Short answers: by default hosted retains logs for a configurable period - we can enable no-retention for certain endpoints; in Dedicated/Private, data isolation is enforced and no cross-tenant sharing. We'll provide the data retention matrix in the docs.
[05:08] Aaron Patel: And encryption-at-rest with customer-managed KMS - is that supported in hosted?
[05:12] Marco Alvarez: Hosted supports envelope encryption with our KMS but we offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private. For hosted enterprise customers we can also discuss bringing your KMS via federated key APIs depending on compliance needs.

[05:30] (Notes on integration)
[05:31] Marco Alvarez: Integration options: 1) Quickstart via hosted API keys - easiest, low friction. 2) Dedicated capacity for throughput and strict isolation. 3) Private/VPC for on-prem or air-gapped. For the pilot we recommend hosted sandbox first, then evaluate dedicated if throughput or data policies require it.
[05:55] Leah Thompson: That makes sense. We'll try hosted sandbox but want the option to move to dedicated within a month or two.

[06:05] (Transcription glitch)
[06:06] Speaker 2: ..um, yeah.. *inaudible* something about cache..

[06:15] (Benchmarks and success criteria)
[06:16] Jordan Lee: To be specific on success criteria: 1) perf: 95th latency under 300ms on short prompts or agreed SLA 2) quality: summaries match current accuracy baseline (we'll accept +/- 5% on key metrics) 3) cost: target is at least 20% improvement vs current spend under similar workload. We'll capture exact KPI thresholds in the pilot plan.
[06:40] Maya Chen: For quality we will provide evaluation prompts and golden labels. Can you run evals and flag regressions automatically?
[06:47] Marco Alvarez: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes continuous eval hooks and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We'll instrument that in the sandbox.

[07:00] (Operational questions)
[07:02] Carlos Ruiz: About SSO: we use Okta for SAML. Does Redwood support SCIM for user provisioning?
[07:07] Priya Nair: Yes, SCIM supported. We'll share the provisioning guide and metadata endpoints.
[07:12] Leah Thompson: For network, if we need to do VPC peering, what's typical lead time?
[07:16] Marco Alvarez: For VPC peering or private endpoints usually 2-3 weeks to coordinate network and firewall rules; Dedicated + Private can take longer if on-premed.

[07:30] (Pricing and procurement)
[07:31] Jordan Lee: High-level pricing options: hosted pay-as-you-go with usage tiers, reserved dedicated monthly commits, private licensing. For the pilot we'll propose an evaluation SKU with discounted usage. I'll include a ballpark in the post-call deck.
[07:48] Carlos Ruiz: We'll need pricing for both hosted pilot and a dedicated 12-month reserved option for budgeting.
[07:54] Jordan Lee: We'll send both.

[08:02] (Next steps recap)
[08:03] Jordan Lee: Recap of immediate next steps: Jordan to share security docs and pricing; Priya to provision sandbox; Marco to schedule perf deep dive and run baseline tests once sample data is in; Aegis to share SSO metadata, sample dataset, and confirm pilot KPIs.
[08:20] Maya Chen: We'll aim to have sample data and SSO details to you in the next week.
[08:23] Aaron Patel: I'll take point for SSO and KMS.

[08:30] (Small interruptions / crosstalk)
[08:31] Speaker 3: sorry - one more question -
[08:33] Leah Thompson: Go ahead.
[08:34] Speaker 3: Do you have a list of supported models and quantization levels?
[08:36] Marco Alvarez: Yes - model catalog link (we will include). We can discuss which quant profiles are most cost-effective for your workload. Sometimes the transcript shows model aliases incorrectly, like 'gpt-4x' vs our open-model names. We'll clarify in the doc.

[09:00] (Wrap-up)
[09:02] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone - great conversation. We'll follow up with the onboarding plan and schedule the SE deep dive.
[09:08] Maya Chen: Thanks - looking forward.
[09:10] Carlos Ruiz: Thanks all.
[09:12] (Meeting ends, informal chat)
[09:20] Priya Nair: I'll send calendar invites for weekly check-ins; default Mon 10am PT unless you prefer otherwise.
[09:26] Leah Thompson: Monday 10am PT works.
